USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Targeting allergic inflammation

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 22-year-old woman has allergic asthma that remains poorly controlled despite appropriate inhaled therapy. A specialist adds omalizumab after confirming eligibility. Which molecular interaction is most directly inhibited by this biologic?

  1. IL-5 binding to its receptor
  2. Acetylcholine binding to muscarinic receptors
  3. Leukotriene binding to the CysLT1 receptor
  4. Cortisol binding to intracellular glucocorticoid receptors
  5. Binding of free IgE to its high-affinity receptor
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Binding of free IgE to its high-affinity receptor

Omalizumab binds free IgE, reducing its availability for receptor binding.

Understanding the options

Binding of free IgE to its high-affinity receptor
Omalizumab binds free IgE, reducing its availability for receptor binding.
IL-5 binding to its receptor
This is the pathway targeted by mepolizumab and reslizumab.
Acetylcholine binding to muscarinic receptors
This is the mechanism of antimuscarinic bronchodilators.
Leukotriene binding to the CysLT1 receptor
This describes montelukast and zafirlukast.
Cortisol binding to intracellular glucocorticoid receptors
Omalizumab does not block glucocorticoid receptors.
